entities.summary:
Huaraz, formerly designated as San Sebastián de Huaraz, is a city in Peru. It is the capital of the Ancash Region and the seat of government of Huaraz Province. The urban area's population is distributed over the districts of Huaraz and Independencia. The city is located in the middle of the Callejon de Huaylas valley and on the right side of the Santa river.

The city has an elevation of approximately 3050 meters above sea level. The built-up area covers 8 square kilometers and has a population of 120,000 inhabitants, making it the second largest city in the central Peruvian Andes after the city of Huancayo. Huaraz is a big city from Americas, created circa 1574-01-30. A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Huaraz was a major center of trade and commerce in the Andean region during the Spanish colonial period, with significant economic and cultural impact on the surrounding communities. Its population has grown to over 120,000 inhabitants, making it a crucial urban hub in the central Peruvian Andes.
